description:
The progress file is stamped `deploymentStatus: "completed"` during the local pass, making the patch script's own gate structurally inert

Classification basis (verbatim from the severity-classifier): Low under C4: no assets at risk and no protocol function or availability impacted. The impact is an off-chain address file, recoverable and backed up, reachable only through three compounded manual deviations after a crashed broadcast. The reportable substance is that a documented safety interlock carries zero information - a real defect, correctly sized at Low.
impact: None on-chain. The blast radius is an OFF-CHAIN artefact: `mainnet-addresses.ts` patched with addresses for contracts that may never have been deployed, which then feeds the UI and downstream scripts.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. `_writeProgressFileWithStatus("completed")` is called at the end of `run()` - the end of forge's LOCAL pass, before any transaction is broadcast.
2. `_trackDeployment`/`_trackConfig` write `"in_progress"` during the same pass, so `"in_progress"` is only ever observable after a LOCAL-pass revert (which also yields a non-zero forge exit).
3. Any run that reaches the broadcast stage at all has therefore already written `"completed"` with every step marked done.

4. `patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js:122-124` gates on exactly `deploymentStatus === 'completed'`, and its header at :16-22 describes that gate as 'necessary but not sufficient'. It is in fact necessary AND unconditionally true at every point the patcher can run - i.e. it carries zero information.

5. Harm requires THREE compounded operator deviations: the broadcast crashes; the operator invokes the patcher manually OUTSIDE the `&&` chain; and the operator skips the documented mandatory hand-trim against run-latest.json receipts.
recommendation:
Either (a) write `"completed"` from the JS side after `forge script` returns 0 - i.e. have `patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js` itself accept an explicit `--confirm-broadcast` flag and stop reading `deploymentStatus` as evidence - or (b) restate the header honestly: 'deploymentStatus is written pre-broadcast and is NOT evidence that anything landed; the only interlocks are the `&&` short-circuit and the mandatory hand-trim against run-latest.json receipts.' Option (b) is a one-line documentation fix and is sufficient.

CLASSIFIER ADDENDUM: whichever option is chosen, apply it to the SHARED idiom rather than this one script - `_writeProgressFileWithStatus` has six users (see MR-22-01) and the paired `patch-mainnet-addresses-*.js` gate exists on at least three of them.
recommendationQuality: strong - two options, one of them a one-line fix the finding itself certifies as sufficient

classification.likelihood: low - the two real interlocks (the `&&` short-circuit and the mandatory hand-trim) are correctly implemented and documented, and `backup-mainnet-addresses.js` runs first in the chain. The plausible trigger is a manual recovery action after a crashed broadcast, which is exactly the moment an operator improvises.
classification.assumptions: An operator who believes `deploymentStatus` is an independent interlock (which the header invites) and who patches manually after a partial broadcast.
classification.externalRequirements: A crashed or partial broadcast, plus manual out-of-chain invocation.
classification.recoverability: Full - `backup-mainnet-addresses.js` precedes the patch in the chain, and the address file is version-controlled.

pocNote: No standalone PoC. Evidence is the run-22 mainnet-fork PREVIEW execution of `promotion-ready:dry` at block 25659373 (see the script-audit review artifacts).

severityDebate.whyHeldAtLow: Re-examined specifically on the grounds that 'the resume path's provenance check carries zero information' on an irreversible operation. Held at Low: (a) the consequence is confined to an off-chain, version-controlled, backed-up address file - no on-chain state, no funds, no availability of a protocol function; (b) the interlock that is inert was never the load-bearing one - the `&&` short-circuit and the mandatory hand-trim both function, so this is a redundant check going quiet, not a control failing; (c) harm needs three compounded manual deviations, which is squarely 'hypothetical with external requirements' rather than a demonstrated impact. Its real cost is EPISTEMIC - an operator over-trusting a flag - and epistemic cost with a working primary control is a Low.
severityDebate.oneShotWeight: Applied as ORDERING (L-03, above four other Lows) rather than as a tier change, because the moment it bites - improvised recovery after a crashed one-shot broadcast - is exactly the moment the one-shot context creates.
severityDebate.crossRunNote: This is the ledger-ANTICIPATED mainnet realisation of 1e8cc0dc, whose note reads 'PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET as a PATTERN'. Filing it at Low confirms the prediction at the same tier the predicting entry carries, which is internally consistent.

basis: Different entryPoint (promotion-ready:broadcast vs dev) => different fingerprint. Reconciles separately by design.
Different contract (DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol vs DeployMocks.s.sol) and different function (run / _writeProgressFileWithStatus vs _writeProgressFile).
Different target: the ledger instance writes progress.31337.json on ANVIL; PR-10 writes the MAINNET progress file a live cutover depends on.

Different consumer, and this is the material addition: PR-10 identifies a downstream JS GATE (patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js:122-124) that reads deploymentStatus === 'completed' as a safety interlock, and a header at :16-22 describing it as 'necessary but not sufficient' when it is in fact necessary AND unconditionally true - i.e. it carries zero information. The ledger's dev instance had no such consumer analysis.

The ledger entry's own note ANTICIPATES this filing ('PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET as a PATTERN'). PR-10 is the predicted mainnet instance arriving; dropping it as a duplicate would erase the confirmation the note was written to invite.
crossEntryPointDisclosurePreservedVerbat.actionForHuman: File PR-10 as new. Consider linking it to 1e8cc0dc as the mainnet realisation of that pattern, so a single hardening of the shared _writeProgressFileWithStatus idiom can close both.
